findings.summary: The recommendation rule is not specified for any proposal that can really exist, so the producer has to guess it, and the rejected 'same answer for every proposal' fault can come back.
findings.evidence: The plan says the recommendation is 'a pure function of rung, role and evidence count' and gives one example: zero evidence gives 'Hold: it cites no evidence'. WorkItem::validate (crates/athena-data/src/records.rs:1880-1882) rejects any non-blind-spot item with empty evidence, so a real proposal never hits that case. No other mapping is written down. Ladder has five rungs (crates/athena-data/src/roles.rs:14-25). In practice, Steward proposals at the same rung with a similar evidence count would get the same text. The criterion-4 test passes as soon as two hand-picked fixtures at different rungs differ, even if every real proposal at one rung gets the same verdict. It is a heuristic presented as a recommendation, with the actual rule left to the producer. Fix: Write the full mapping into the plan, and base it on data the code has. For example, one line per Ladder rung that says who must decide and why: the role's limit is in roles.rs, and athena-core has role_limit, but xtask cannot reach that crate, so say what stands in for it. Name the action the owner takes (`athena approve-work <id>` / `athena reject-work <id>`) and the evidence to read first. Or decide that the honest line is 'Recommendation: none recorded by the proposal; decide with approve-work or reject-work' plus the evidence pointer. Then make the criterion-4 test assert the exact expected line for each fixture, not just that the two lines differ.
findings.location: Plan decision 4 and step 4 (`recommendation(item)`); demonstration for criterion 4

findings.summary: On the published site the page will show 'records branch not in this checkout' and no briefs, so the request's 'render briefs from the real waiting proposals on the site' is not yet true on the site.
findings.evidence: .github/workflows/pages.yml checks out main only (actions/checkout with no fetch of athena/records). resolve_tip (crates/athena-git/src/records_branch.rs:55-84) returns Missing when neither refs/heads/athena/records nor refs/remotes/origin/athena/records exists. The plan says so honestly, and workflows are out of scope in the accepted reading. Fix: Say this in the CHANGELOG entry too, for example 'the live page lists briefs once the pages workflow fetches athena/records (follow-up)', so the change is not read as delivering live briefs. Ask Athena to queue the workflow follow-up as its own job.

findings.summary: The tip may come from a local branch with commits that were never pushed, so links pinned to it can 404.
findings.evidence: resolve_tip prefers the local ref when it descends from the tracking ref (records_branch.rs:68-73). Local-only records commits are not on GitHub. Fix: When `from` is RECORDS_REF and a tracking ref exists, say on the page that links point at the local tip, or pin to the tracking tip when the two differ. A one-line note in the page shell is enough.

findings.summary: Repeating the title as 'what it would change' costs about 12 counted words per brief and adds nothing.
findings.evidence: WorkItem has only `title` as one-line text (records.rs:1861-1862). The label alone is about 12 words of the 120-word budget. Fix: Render the line as 'What it would change: not recorded beyond the title above' (shorter), or fold it into the title row.

summary: I checked the code the plan relies on. The plan is grounded and mostly sound. Everything it names exists with the shapes it assumes: `records_branch::resolve_tip` returning Missing/At/Diverged; `Git::ls_tree_under`, which is recursive; `cat_blobs`; `Git::at`/`run`/`discover`; `check_record_file`; the WorkItem and WorkDecision fields, including `work_item: RecordId`; `AnyRecord::canonical_path` with the work-items and work-decisions paths; and the private `source_url`, `ATHENA_URL` and `CSS` in site.rs. xtask already depends on athena-data and athena-git. The open filter matches athena-core's `open_proposals`: kind Proposal, no decision, sorted by `at` then id. Reading only the records-branch tip, with no HEAD fallback, is well argued. The empty, missing and unparseable states stay distinct, and the demonstrations call real functions with real temp-git fixtures and no doubles. The new index paragraph does not break the order checks in site_page.rs. One major soundness gap remains. The recommendation is described as derived from rung, role and evidence count, but the only rule given (zero evidence gives 'Hold') can never apply to a real proposal, because validate() requires evidence. The rule for real proposals is left to the producer, and the criterion-4 test only checks that two chosen fixtures differ. The planner should write the full mapping, or an explicit 'none recorded' line plus the owner's action, and test the exact output. The minor points: the live site will show no briefs until a workflow follow-up lands, which should be flagged; and links pinned to a local tip may not resolve on GitHub.
